chapter: His own groups, compositions and friends
title: Janos Starker
summary: Baker calls Starker the greatest cellist, whose 1949 Kodaly recording set the standard, and says political disagreements do not affect their friendship.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Janos Starker, the greatest cellist that has ever lived, I think the most important cellist of all time, in the sense that the development of the cello had really stopped right about the time of Pablo Casals. Starker, with his 1949 recording of the Kodaly unaccompanied [Sonata for Unaccompanied Cello], set a standard that was so high, that
now that’s the measuring stick for virtually everything. Plus he’s a very, very good friend. We differ about a lot of things politically, but they don’t get in the way of our friendship.
